title: Consumer inbox: one local effect for a repeated event
outcome: Commit deduplication and projection changes together, then acknowledge Kafka progress.
benefits: Repeat-safe local effects across process crashes.
drawbacks: External side effects need additional boundaries.
version: Kafka 4.1 KRaft · lab Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 · legacy Rails adaptation notes

trace.title: Validated event
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A consumer can receive a record again after a crash/rebalance/replay. A seen? query followed by a write races when two processes overlap.

Use a unique consumer-specific event key at the authority that stores the effect.

An inbox row and projection update in one DB transaction make the local effect repeat-safe: either both commit or neither does. A later Kafka offset commit remains a separate step.

If that commit fails, replay checks the inbox and avoids repeating the local projection.

This does not atomically include email, another database, or every external API. Each side-effect boundary needs its own intent/idempotency/reconciliation design.

“Exactly once” must name the scope where it is enforced.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Receive E → validate → insert inbox + update report → commit DB → commit Kafka.

Crash after DB commit before Kafka commit: receive E again → unique inbox says local effect exists → do not repeat it → commit progress.

Include consumer identity in deduplication scope when different projections independently need the same event. Their completion responsibilities are separate.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
Writing inbox before the effect in a separate committed transaction can lose the effect. Writing it after can duplicate.

A memory Set disappears on process restart.
